requirements.text: A layer MUST import only from layers below it and from the `contracts` package. The engine (L4) and the pass loop (L3) MUST import interfaces of L2 and never an implementation of L1. The build MUST fail when an import-boundary check over the package graph finds a violation. (LR-1)

A host MUST reach the product only through the CLI protocol of annex G. A host MUST NOT read a state file, an event file, a launch contract or a log. Diagnosis by a host MUST go through a CLI command whose output has a byte cap. (LR-2)

Between the CLI (L6) and the runtime root (L5) there MUST be only files, one start of the runtime root at launch, and signals for `stop --now`. The CLI MUST write only the files that the table of annex B §B.5 gives it as writer: requests to the inbox, launch records, the supervision record, and the records of a launch and of a reverse plan that are written before a runtime exists. It MUST NOT write run state. (LR-3)

Only the runtime tree (the runtime root and the engine) MUST write the control plane, with the exceptions of F100-FR-003. A reader MUST derive the conditions `dead`, `stale` and `launch-abandoned`; no process writes them as a state. (LR-4)

At any moment exactly one process MUST be the writer of a run's event file: the runtime root while no engine is alive, the engine while it is alive. Learning MUST have its own writer domain, its own lock and its own event file. The rule MUST be tested under contention in Wave 1. (LR-5)

Every process boundary that the parity oracle observes at the baselines MUST stay a process boundary. Every other boundary MUST be a call that returns a result record whose `exit_code` field carries the same code number as the as-is process. The tables of annex E §E.4 and annex G §G.4 are the authority on which is which. (LR-6)

The router, the quota classifier, the relaunch classifier, lane derivation and the terms gate MUST each be a pure table: versioned data, evaluated by the one table evaluator of annex X §X.3, with the rule id and the table version recorded with every decision. (LR-7)

Role resolution MUST belong to the harness layer. It MUST run at launch and produce a plan per phase and per role, with the fallbacks the consumer opted into, each entry checked by the terms gate again at the moment it is used. A loop layer or a router MUST NOT call role resolution. (LR-8)
requirements.parity: off: no fallback is configured (row 40 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Text from outside the runtime (a harness stream, the output of a check, a critic reply, the consumer's comment) MUST enter through one ingress, where it is redacted by the redactor of annex X §X.4 and cut to a size cap. Sinks and prompts MUST receive only the result. Under the `parity` profile the cap MUST NOT be below the as-is sizes that reach the critic prompt (phase evidence up to 60000 characters; a grounding budget of 327680 bytes at a window of 200000 tokens), or FX-25 differs. (LR-9)

Every switch of the product MUST be ordinary product configuration. The parity configuration MUST be the named profile `parity` of annex X §X.7, which sets every switch the oracle needs. The product MUST have no oracle mode and no code path that exists only for the oracle, other than the compatibility projection, which consumers may also switch on. (LR-10)

Every closed set MUST be listed in annex X §X.6 with its owner and its rule for an unknown value. Every file of the control plane MUST carry a `schema` field, and a reader MUST refuse a file whose major differs from the one it supports. (LR-11)

The core packages (the engine with the pass loop, and every loop-layer package) MUST import the `contracts` package and the kernel package of shared pure helpers and nothing else from the product. They MUST NOT import a harness adapter, a sink adapter, a config loader, a host package, a UI package or a provider SDK, and they MUST NOT start a process or open a network connection directly. They MUST NOT import the file-system module of the platform: a core package reads and writes files through the kernel and through the ports of the edge packages (F100-FR-234). The import-boundary check MUST enforce this, and MUST fail when a core file names a sample implementation or a Wave 1 implementation of any extension point.
requirements.assumption: CQ-185 (whether a core package may import the file-system module; read as no)

requirements.text: The kernel package MUST offer to the core what the core may not import: a process primitive with the operations start a process in a group and a session of its own, with standard input closed and, where the caller names them, two files as its standard output and standard error; start such a process detached with a status record, in which the kernel starts a waiter of its own in the new session, with no shell, and the waiter starts the command, waits for its end and writes its exit code or signal, its duration and its times of start and end atomically to a file the caller names, so that the record exists when the process that started it has ended (the baseline does the same with a wrapper, B-1127, B-1070); signal a group (polite, terminate, kill), read the start time of a process, search the process table for a run token, and wait for an end; a clock; the registration call of the doctor's checks; and the atomic write. The core and every loop layer MUST receive these as arguments from the composition root. An edge package MAY touch the file system or start a process on behalf of a core package, behind an interface of the `contracts` package: in Wave 1 one for the integrity of checks (owner 116), one for the tree store (owner 143) and one for the check runner (owner 148).

Each extension point MUST have an id of the form `specstride.<name>/<major>`. A change inside a major MUST be additive. An implementation MUST declare the majors it supports; the registry MUST refuse an implementation outside the supported range and the doctor MUST report it. The core MUST support the current major and the one before it.

An implementation MUST be of one of three classes: data (a file validated against a schema), first-party code (a package of the product that registers through the registration call), or third-party code (a package named in user configuration). Wave 1 MUST accept data from consumers and first-party code from the product. Third-party code MUST be refused at registration in Wave 1, with a message that names the class; its interface is designed and not enabled.

An implementation that widens capability MUST be accepted from user configuration, the environment or flags only, and never from project configuration. A widening entry in project configuration MUST be ignored with a launch message and a doctor warning.

Each extension point MUST have one registry, filled at process start and read-only after launch. What a run resolved from a registry MUST be written to the run's records and replayed on resume; a resume MUST NOT resolve again unless the consumer asks for it by flag.

Each extension point MUST have a conformance suite in the published test kit. Every Wave 1 implementation MUST pass its suite in the build. A data implementation MUST be validated when it is loaded, and the consumer MUST be able to run the conformance suite on it on request.

For each extension point EP-01 to EP-19 the test tree MUST hold a sample implementation outside the core. The build MUST run the conformance suite on the sample and MUST fail if any core file names the sample. Adding or removing the sample MUST change no core file.

An implementation that throws, exceeds its time limit or returns a value outside the closed result set of its point MUST be degraded to the plainer path that the section of that point documents. A failing implementation MUST NOT produce a verdict, an exit code or a stop reason of its own. The degradation MUST be recorded as an event.

EP-01 to EP-17 and EP-19 MUST be public interface contracts with a compatibility promise per major. EP-18 MUST be an internal seam: versioned and tested in the same way, with a conformance suite and a sample, and with no promise to implementers outside the product's repository in Wave 1.

Every extension point MUST state what the core does with a value it does not know. Where the section of a point states nothing more specific, the rule MUST be: an unknown field is ignored by a reader and kept by a writer that copies the record; an unknown member of a closed set refuses the record with a message that names the set and the value; an unknown member of an open set is resolved through the registry and refused only if no entry matches.

The calls of the engine into learning MUST be a plain function interface of the `contracts` package at layer L2, which the composition root hands to the engine. The interface MUST have five operations: `resolve` a value and its arm for a knob and a phase at the start of a pass; `observe` an approved phase; `evaluate` the applied decisions of an approved phase; `report` the last recorded evaluation of every active decision, read-only, for the lines printed at exit; and the tamper bracket as two operations, `bracketTake` before a proposer pass and `bracketCheck` after it (F100-FR-228). It is no extension point in Wave 1. A failure of a call MUST leave the run on the value it would have had without learning, and MUST never undo an approval.

The calls of the engine into the invocation code of feature 126 (`reconcile` the observations of one invocation into a result, `finalize` one invocation into the result, its event and a decision of the closed set of row 175 of annex X §X.6, `sweepRetention` of the invocations of a run) MUST be a plain function interface of the `contracts` package at layer L2, which the composition root hands to the engine. It is no extension point in Wave 1. `finalize` takes the invocation identity, the breaker state, the limit, an optional kill reason and an optional cap limit, and returns the decision, the reason code, `is_error`, the count of consecutive errors, the kill class and the cap count (F126-FR-034). The implementation is in `@specstride/harness` (feature 126); the caller is the pass loop (feature 103, F103-FR-013).

Every specification of the product MUST use the terms of the glossary with one meaning each. A term that the glossary marks "never bare" MUST be written in its qualified form: phase gate, launch check, verification gate, phase attempt, stage attempt, launch contract, launch bundle, spec bundle, engine hook, host hook, harness adapter, auth tier, model tier. The old use of "micro-loop" for diagnosis and acceleration MUST be written "recovery cycle".

A requirement of any feature MUST NOT assume a closed list of harnesses. Anything that enumerates harnesses MUST read the resolved registry, which includes discovered harnesses and harnesses the consumer declared. The core MUST NOT test a harness name in control flow.

The critic MUST never approve its own session. Every critic call MUST run in a fresh session. Where the critic and the proposer resolve to the same model, the critic-diversity warning MUST be raised and recorded, and it MUST NOT block a run. The warning MUST also be raised where the diversity test gives `unverified`.

The product MUST behave the same on Linux and on macOS for every requirement of this specification. Windows and WSL MUST be reported by the doctor as unvalidated. Every statement about macOS in every feature is `unverified` until a macOS runner has passed the parity oracle, which is a release condition.

requirements.text: The product MUST NOT read state written by the three as-is systems. An old state tree found in a workspace MUST be reported by the doctor and left untouched. Legacy command names, legacy variable names and migrations of a pre-v2 layout MUST NOT be carried.

The product MUST be delivered as one published package that holds the CLI, the entry of the runtime and the host package for Claude Code. The `contracts` package and the test kit MUST be published as well. Installing any of them MUST run no install script and MUST compile nothing. Every dependency of a published package MUST be declared at an exact version, never a range (the control of threat T-44).
requirements.assumption: CQ-206 (the "exact versions" part of the control of T-44 is anchored in this requirement; no requirement id is spent on it)

requirements.text: The package as shipped MUST have the audience `distributed`. The audience MUST change only through user configuration, and never through the environment, a flag, project configuration or the consumer's comment (ruling 2).
requirements.assumption: CQ-205 (ruling 2 is read to name user configuration as the one source of the audience)

requirements.text: The licence of the product MUST be MIT, with the copyright line "Copyright (c) 2026 mairp". A published file MUST NOT hold a path, an account or a name that is specific to the owner's machines. Every dependency MUST be compatible with MIT; a proprietary dependency MUST be optional and never bundled.

Every component of the product MUST be written in the one language the owner ruled. A component in another language MUST enter only through an entry in the Language Ledger, which is empty at the start of Wave 1.

The micro-loop layer, the layer of parallel units and concurrent verification commands MUST add no run state, no exit code and no stop reason. Every failure inside them MUST end in one of: the work returns to the serial path; the layer is off for the phase attempt; the layer is off for the run.

The product MUST keep state in exactly three roots (user-level state, the control plane of the workspace, the workspace part) and, with parallel units on, in the worker root, as in the table of §B.1. The control plane MUST lie outside the working tree. A mutable file MUST NOT be shared between two workspaces.

The worker root MUST lie outside the workspace and outside the control plane. The tree store MUST lie in the control plane of the run. The worker root and the tree store MUST NOT exist when parallel units are off. Both MUST be removed when the run ends.

A control root inside the working tree MUST be accepted only together with a deny rule for the proposer's harness, and the run MUST then record `protection=detect` unless the harness adapter confirms the denial.

requirements.text: A file in the workspace part MUST NOT decide anything. The runtime MUST read the outbox and the phase evidence as claims, after the pass has exited, as regular files and without following links. (SL-1)

Every file the runtime writes MUST be written to a temporary name in the same directory and renamed into place, so that no reader sees a partial file. A state file MUST hold current state only; history is the event stream. (SL-2)

Grounding MUST refuse, by real path, every path of the control plane, of the event stream, of the outbox, of the carry-over files (the handoff and the proposer's notebook), of the worker root and of the tree store, and every path under the project's repository directory, whatever the phase evidence cites and whether a loop layer is on or off. (SL-3)

Feature 100 MUST own one table from logical names to locations, with a layout version. Specifications, the parity oracle, the doctor and messages to the consumer MUST name state by logical name. A change of layout MUST change that table and the layout version and nothing else in any specification. (SL-4)

After launch, the inbox MUST be the only place where a process outside the runtime tree writes, apart from the supervision record of §B.16. A stop request MUST be honoured as at the baseline, including when it was written while no run was active. (SL-5)

At containment levels C0 and C1 the control plane is protected by its location and by detection, not by the operating system. The run record and the `[LOOP]` line MUST then say `protection=detect`. At C2 and above they MUST say `protection=prevent` only when the harness adapter confirmed that the sandbox denies writes to the control plane. (SL-6)
State trees of the three as-is systems MUST NOT be read. The workspace part MUST carry a layout version file, so that it can be told apart from an old tree of the same name. (SL-7)

While a run is alive the runtime root MUST keep an advisory marker in the workspace part that holds the owner record of §B.9. A launch that finds a marker whose owner it cannot probe MUST be refused with `foreign-owner`. The marker is a safety measure and decides nothing else; its removal by a pass MUST be reported as an integrity event.

Directories of the control plane, of the user-level state and of the worker root MUST be readable and writable by their owner only, and files likewise. The runtime MUST resolve real paths and require them to stay inside their root, MUST refuse a symbolic link inside the control plane, and MUST open files it reads as claims without following links.

When the learning mode is not `off`, the engine MUST, before each proposer pass, record the size and the hash of the leading bytes of three files that the proposer could reach: the event stream of the run, the decision log of learning and the observation of the current phase; and MUST check after the pass that those leading bytes are unchanged. Appends are allowed. A file that shrank, or whose leading bytes changed, MUST give one event `integrity.events_changed` with the phase, the phase attempt and the file, and MUST mark the run as left out of every baseline and every evaluation of learning. The engine executes the bracket through the calls of F100-FR-235; the rule and its thresholds belong to feature 106 (F106-FR-037).
The identifiers of §B.3 MUST be minted by the process named there, with the scope and the rule named there. Every record and every event that concerns an identified thing MUST carry its identifiers.

A `launch` MUST continue the unfinished run of the same feature, with its `runId` and its counts, and MUST say so in one line. A new run MUST start only when no unfinished run of the feature exists or when the consumer passes `--new-run`. Counts inside a run MUST be reset only by `--reset-counts`, which is accepted from the command line only and is never stored in the run snapshot.
requirements.parity: resume fixtures pass `--reset-counts` (row 13 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Where the compatibility projection or compatibility output shows the as-is run id, it MUST show a value of the as-is form: date and time of the engine start to the second, a hyphen, and the process id of the engine.

The logical name of anything that belongs to a phase attempt MUST carry the phase number, the ordinal of the engine start and the ordinal of the phase attempt, so that the name stays unique when counts were reset. Where a directory of that name already exists, the as-is suffix rule MUST apply: the run id is appended.

Every file of the control plane and every record of §B.7 to §B.18 MUST carry a field `schema` whose value is the schema id with its major, for example `specstride.lease/1`. A file of several records MUST carry it in every record.

A reader MUST refuse a record whose schema id it does not know or whose major differs from the one it supports, with a message that names the logical name, the major found and the major supported, and with a doctor finding. `resume` on a run whose records have a different major MUST refuse with exit 3. A reader MUST ignore a field it does not know. A writer MUST add fields inside a major only in an additive way.
The run record MUST hold the version of the product that started the run and the version of every later engine start. A difference MUST be recorded as an event and shown by the doctor.

Every state file MUST have exactly one writing process, named in the table of §B.5. Two processes MUST never write the same state file. Where two processes need to record state about one thing, each MUST have its own file.

A record of this annex MUST NOT hold a secret value, a nonce before its call has returned, or prompt or reply content. A secret is stored as its reference; a nonce as its hash; content as a logical name with hash and size.

The table of §B.5 MUST be the complete list of logical names of Wave 1, each with its root, its one writer and its readers. A feature that needs a name the table does not hold MUST NOT invent one: it reports the need, and the name is added here with a new minor of the layout version.
requirements.assumption: CQ-018 (the spelling of every logical name other than `gate:<N>:approved`, `attempt:…:evidence`, `run:<id>:events`, `worker-root` and `tree-store`, which the sources give)

requirements.text: The five compared logs and records of the as-is pipeline runtime and supervisor, and the engine log, MUST have the logical names `pipeline:<pipelineId>:launcher-log`, `pipeline:<pipelineId>:report-log`, `pipeline:<pipelineId>:launch-log`, `pipeline:<pipelineId>:harness-run` and `run:<runId>:engine-log`. The compatibility projection MUST write them as files, so that the oracle compares them by logical name. The engine log MUST be written once per engine start, under `run:<runId>:engine-log:<k>`, and the bare name `run:<runId>:engine-log` MUST resolve to the newest engine start, as for `run:<runId>:events-legacy:<k>` (F100-FR-229).
requirements.parity: written (the compatibility projection is on) (row 17 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The names `workspace:current:events` and `workspace:current:engine-log` MUST resolve to the event file and the engine log of the newest engine start of the workspace, and the state of a feature MUST be reachable under the feature slug. They take the place of the as-is links at the top of the state directory and of the as-is directories per feature and per run.

The old side of the layout table (as-is path to logical name, for each of the two baselines) MUST be part of the normalization contract of annex X §X.8, fixed by the `file` rows of the behaviour inventory. It MUST map the as-is approval marker to `gate:<N>:approved`.

At the start of every phase the engine MUST look for a stray notebook of the proposer at the two as-is stray places (the directory of the phase evidence and the root of the working tree) and move it to `feature:<slug>:notebook`. The newer file wins: the stray file is deleted when the canonical file is newer, and replaces it otherwise. The engine MUST write the as-is log line of the sweep with both paths.

For every sweep of F100-FR-057 the engine MUST emit the event `progress.swept`, and the compatibility projection MUST render it as the as-is event of the sweep with the fields `from` (the stray path) and `to` (the canonical path).

The as-is event file MUST be written once per engine start, under `run:<runId>:events-legacy:<k>`. The consumer's comment MUST be kept verbatim, after redaction, under `launch:<launchId>:comment`, and the launch record MUST hold only its hash. A shell shim of a host MUST find the precomputed status line through `workspace:current:status-line`, whose place depends on the real path of the workspace only.

The workspace record MUST hold the fields above. A launch whose lock provider differs from the recorded one MUST be refused with a doctor finding. A launch in a workspace whose spec shows ticked phases that have no approval record MUST be refused and MUST name the commands `state export`, `state import` and `state adopt`.

The launch record MUST hold the fields above and MUST be written before the detach strategy is called. A launch record older than the handshake limit that has no `outcome` and no lease with its nonce MUST be derived by readers as `launch-abandoned`, shown as an attention item, and closed by the next launch.
requirements.assumption: CQ-019 (fields beyond mode, comment hash, detach strategy and launch nonce, which the sources name)

requirements.text: The lease MUST hold the fields above. Liveness MUST be read from the lease through the lock provider and MUST never be an event. A reader MUST derive `dead` when the run record shows a live state and the lease has no live owner, and `stale` when the owner lives and both the heartbeat and the newest event are old.
The owner record MUST hold the fields above. It is part of the lease, of the lock and of the advisory marker. A lock MUST never exist without an owner record.
requirements.status: unverified (check: resolution of the process start time and the boot identity on macOS; verified-on: —; pin: —)

requirements.text: The process registry MUST hold one entry per child process, with the fields above. Processes of a pass, of a critic-class call, of a check, of a stage and of a worker MUST be of class `owned`. The detached job of an accepted yield and a long verification job MUST be of class `adoptable`, with the kind `detached-job`; no process of a worker is ever `adoptable`.

A stop and `stop --now` MUST end `owned` processes only, and only after pid, start time and run token all match. An `adoptable` process MUST survive a stop, MUST NOT make the lock provider report `owner-dead-group-alive`, and MUST be adopted by the next engine start; ending one MUST be a separate, explicit request. When the engine exits for any cause, the runtime root MUST end every `owned` process before it relaunches or rests.

The inbox MUST accept exactly the three request types above. An empty stop request MUST mean a clean stop with every default. The engine MUST read the stop request at the boundaries of the baseline and during a pass, and MUST remove it when it honours it. A host event MUST inform only: it never pauses, stops or relaunches a run by itself.
requirements.assumption: CQ-019 (field names of the three request types)

requirements.text: The run snapshot MUST hold every resolved key with its source and its class, and the source hashes of the run as pinned values. A failed write of the snapshot MUST be a launch error. Secret references MUST be stored as references. On `resume`, a pinned key MUST rank below flags and above the environment, and a tunable key MUST rank below the environment.

The source hashes MUST be compared with the snapshot at launch of a continued run, at `resume` and at the start of every pass. For the task list the hash that ignores checkboxes MUST be the one compared. A change MUST stop the run with the blocked-on-human signal, name the file, and leave phase evidence that was delivered in place. Under the `parity` profile the three check points MUST NOT be active, and the plan MUST be checked when the critic starts, as at the baseline.
requirements.parity: check at critic start only (row 15 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: A run MUST have one ledger: append-only, every record chained to the one before and signed with a key that is not the approval key. With every loop layer off it MUST hold at least one record per phase attempt. A truncated, reordered or edited ledger MUST be detected; the effect is that every loop layer is off for the phase attempt, and never a stop.
requirements.assumption: CQ-019 (field names of the envelope; the sources name the properties and the fields `pass_id`, `attempt_id`, `tree_hash`, check durations and `session_id`)

requirements.text: The counts that limit a run MUST live in the ledger and MUST continue across a resume and a relaunch: reject counts, ordinals of phase attempts, the MALFORMED streak, pass index, yield index, the consecutive breakers, and the counters of every loop layer. The oscillation window MUST be keyed by the sequence of phase attempts. `--reset-counts` MUST reset them all and MUST be recorded.
requirements.parity: resume fixtures pass `--reset-counts` (row 13 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The runtime MUST accept an approval only from a record it wrote itself, signed with the approval key of the feature and bound to the verdict, the hash of the phase evidence, the result of the verification gate and the tree fingerprint. `resume` MUST verify the signature and every binding; a record that fails, and a bare marker without a record, MUST count as not approved and MUST raise an integrity event. Approval records MUST survive runs.

The engine MUST write the terminal record before it exits, on every exit path. The runtime root, the pipeline stage executor and both relaunch classifier tables MUST read the record and MUST NOT match a stop reason by string in the event file. When the record is missing they MUST classify the end as a crash from the exit code and write a synthesized record.

The cadence state of supervision and, with `relaunch.owner: supervise`, the relaunch budget and the list of relaunches MUST be kept in the supervision record, written by the CLI. It is the only file of run-related state that the CLI writes after launch, apart from inbox requests.

The pause record MUST exist exactly while the run is in the state `paused-quota`, and there MUST be one per run whatever the number of workers. A start of the engine that finds a pause record MUST enter the pause again and compute the remaining wait from `resumeAt` and `ceilingAt`, never from a timer.

On a breach of the integrity of the phase gate the runtime MUST write the tripwire record. While it exists, every run on the machine MUST run with every loop layer off, announced, until the operator clears the tripwire by a command. Clearing MUST remove the record and MUST be recorded as an event in the next run.
requirements.assumption: CQ-019 (field names)

requirements.text: The control plane of a feature MUST be movable: `state export` writes a signed archive (schema id `specstride.state-archive/1`) of the approval records, the ledger and the learning log of one feature; `state import` verifies and installs it; `state adopt` takes over the control plane of the same working tree at an old path. The three commands MUST NOT run while a run of the feature is alive.

Every record of the table of §B.20 MUST carry its schema id and follow the common rules of §B.4. The feature named as owner MUST list the fields in its specification and deliver the schema file to the `contracts` package. A feature that reads such a record MUST read it by its logical name and through its schema, and MUST NOT depend on a field that the owner's specification does not list. In compatibility output and in the compatibility projection the as-is name of a record MUST be written where the baseline writes it.
requirements.assumption: CQ-105; CQ-114 (the schema ids; the queue recommends that feature 100 gives them)

requirements.text: The harness port MUST offer the eight operations `detect`, `capabilities`, `preflight`, `startPass`, `complete`, `stop`, `betweenPasses` and `classify`, with the inputs, outputs and errors of §C.1. It MUST have two capability levels: `proposer` (the harness ends by itself; takes the prompt by standard input, file or bounded argument; works in a given directory without asking; has a declared way to suppress prompts; gives an exit code; lets its credential be checked without a paid call) and `completion` (one prompt in, one reply out; no tools, by construction or by a declared and verified mechanism, or the second form of §C.3; a known context window with its source; a fresh session per call; typed failures; identity of provider and model).

Every capability value MUST carry its provenance, one of `declared`, `probed`, `adapter`, `catalogue`, or MUST be null. A capability that no run has shown MUST be reported as `unverified`. Where a declared and an effective context window differ, the smaller MUST be used.

The proposer MUST come from a flag, the environment, configuration or the shipped default only. When the proposer is absent the launch MUST be refused and the refusal MUST name the discovered candidates. Discovery MUST never change the proposer.
requirements.parity: every fixture names the proposer and the critic (row 36 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The environment of every harness call MUST be an allow-list: the search path, the locale, the home or its overlay, the harness's own auth variables and what the descriptor names. A harness MUST NOT inherit the consumer's other provider keys. The credentials of the critic MUST never be in the environment of the proposer, and the reverse.

A harness executable MUST be resolved to an absolute path at launch and recorded with its version. An executable inside the workspace or in a directory that everyone may write MUST be refused. A path that changed since the last run MUST give a warning.

A transport MUST be a property of a harness adapter. One harness adapter MAY offer several, from the closed set `subprocess`, `sdk-in-process`, `direct-call`, each with its own auth tier and its own row of terms-gate data. A transport whose optional dependency is absent MUST be unavailable, with a doctor line, and MUST leave the other transports untouched. A transport other than the default MUST be chosen by the consumer in user configuration, the environment or a flag, and never automatically.
requirements.parity: `subprocess` for every harness; the critic of each harness in its as-is transport and mode (rows 27, 28 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: A new phase attempt, a critic-class call, a relaunch, a kill by a watchdog, the second repair of a unit, an escalation, a change of configuration and the first pass of the main line after a parallel group was applied MUST each start a fresh session. requirements.text: The harness descriptor MUST hold the fields of §C.2. It MUST be data only: argument lists are lists and never shell text. An unknown top-level key MUST refuse the descriptor; keys under `x-` MUST be ignored. A descriptor whose `descriptorVersion` is outside the accepted range MUST be refused with a doctor finding.

A harness MUST be in one of the four states `tested`, `locally-verified`, `declared`, `detected`. A harness that is not `tested` is unverified: it has no version pin, its capabilities are declared or probed, it runs at auth tier 1 or 2 only, and the doctor shows it as unverified. A descriptor MUST be accepted from user configuration, the environment, flags and the product's bundled data only.

A secret MUST be sent only to the host it was declared for. A plain, unencrypted endpoint MUST be refused unless it is the loopback address. Redirects MUST be refused. A free read-only request to a model list MAY carry the credential; the value MUST never be stored or logged.

The `completion` level MUST have exactly the two forms of §C.3. A critic-class call whose proof is missing or fails MUST be refused with `critic_not_toolless`. A critic path MUST NOT ever receive a flag that allows all tools. The result of the proof MUST be recorded for every critic-class call.
requirements.parity: the critic of each harness in its as-is transport and mode (row 28 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: A critic of either form MUST receive the grounding snapshot and, where one exists, the fact block in its prompt, and its verdict MUST be bound to the nonce of the call. Before a critic of the second form starts, the runtime MUST move the proposer's notebook, handoff and outbox out of the working tree, and MUST move them back after the call. The move holds for every critic-class call, the diagnostician included. The second form is a stated exception to the rules that the critic judges from the grounding snapshot only and holds no tools, and it is limited to reading project files.

The proof of a critic-class call MUST show that the call ran in a session of its own, in one of three ways, and MUST record which: (1) the harness takes a session id from the caller, and the initial record shows the id that the runtime minted; (2) the harness gives the id itself, and the id of the initial record equals no session id of any pass of the run; (3) the initial record carries no session, and the weaker proof applies, for a tested harness adapter only: the exact version pin, the preflight of that harness adapter and the flag set of the call, recorded for every call that rests on it as the weaker proof (§C.3, first form). A proof that fails MUST refuse a configured critic with `critic_not_toolless`, which halts the run, and MUST pass over an automatically picked one. Under the `parity` profile no proof is made, as at the baseline.
requirements.parity: no proof is made for any harness: the as-is transport and mode of each harness, which made no proof (row 28 of annex X §X.7), and `harnesses.dsh.critic.proof` = `none` (row 117 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: A critic MUST run only on a model whose context window is known. A window that the consumer declares (`roles.critic.contextTokens`, or the window of a model in `harnesses.<id>.contextWindows`) MUST always win, and where a declared and an effective window differ the smaller MUST be used. A model whose window is not known MUST NOT qualify for an automatic pick. Outside the `parity` profile, a critic that the consumer configured on a model that is not listed and for which the consumer declares no window MUST be refused by the harness adapter; a fallback window MUST NOT be used. Under the `parity` profile the as-is fallback window of each harness MUST apply to such a critic (128,000, 200,000 or 98,304 tokens, as the baseline of that harness has it; DV-106, DV-111).

requirements.text: There MUST be one registry from `stream.format` to a stream reader. A reader MUST produce only the six normalized records. A reader MUST parse only the harness's own framing, MUST never read the output of a tool as a stream record, MUST enforce a cap on line size and rate, and MUST report a stream that ends without a terminal record. A new stream format MUST be addable as data through `stream.mapping`, with no code.

The harness adapters of pi and prime MUST share one JSONL reader, and what differs between them MUST be data in the dialect table of §C.5. A stream whose session header names a version outside `schemaVersions` MUST be refused. Where `terminalDecides` is true, the outcome of a call MUST be taken from the terminal record.

requirements.text: Role resolution MUST write the resolved registry and role plan with the fields of §C.6 at launch. The engine MUST walk the plan; a resolution MUST NOT take place after launch. A resume or relaunch MUST read the record and MUST NOT rank again unless the consumer asks by flag or the stored pick no longer exists.

An automatically picked critic MUST follow the four steps of §C.6. An unverified harness of kind `cli` MUST never be picked automatically. A harness whose terms are unknown and that the consumer did not name MUST never be a default and MUST never be picked automatically; it is usable when the consumer names it, with the unknown-terms warning. requirements.text: Roles MUST be an open registry: a role has an id, the capability level it needs, its independence constraints against other roles, and its budget key. Role resolution MUST resolve every registered role.

The spec-format port MUST offer the operations `detect`, `parse`, `validate`, `tick` and `inputs` of §C.7 and MUST produce the canonical spec model with structured tasks. Every component that reads a specification MUST read the canonical model; a second parser MUST NOT exist.
The format names and the detection order MUST be those of the Specstride baseline. An explicit format `openspec` MUST be accepted as `openspec-change`.

The check runner MUST be handle-based with the operations `pin`, `start`, `poll`, `result`, `cancel` and `environment` of §C.8, and MUST return the result with each condition in a field of its own. The verification gate, inner checks, the closing check and the merge check MUST use the same runner.

Around every command of the verification gate and around the grounding pass the protected set MUST be fingerprinted before and after. A difference MUST become a fact for the critic and MUST NOT halt the run. A result obtained against a changed set MUST carry the condition `tainted`.

requirements.text: Concurrency of verification commands MUST be a parameter, `verification.parallelism`, with the default 1 and the ceiling 4. A command MUST run beside another only when the check manifest declares the reads and the writes of both and neither reads what the other writes. An undeclared command MUST run alone. A command that fails in a batch of more than one MUST be run once more alone, and both results MUST be stated.

requirements.text: The step runner MUST be an option, `verification.step_runner`, that is off by default. Steps are fixed argument lists run by the runtime, which stops at the first failed required step and can resume from it. A resumed run of steps is partial and MUST never count as evidence of a pass.

requirements.text: A command that is staged before the verification gate MAY be reused by the verification gate only under the reuse policy that its declaration names (`per-attempt`, `per-phase`, `per-run`) and only while the tree is provably the tree of the staged run: the same revision, and a clean working tree in the record of the staged run and at the verification gate, as at the baseline (B-1128). The result of a staged command MUST be kept under `attempt:<N>:<k>:<n>:prestage`. With a loop layer engaged in the phase attempt, that is, with a unit of work declared in it (annex D, F100-FR-118), the verification gate MUST reuse nothing. The engine MUST hand this fact to the verification gate as an input of its call; the verification gate reads no record of a loop layer. The rules are stated by the owner of the verification gate (F105-FR-033).

A verification-plan source MUST offer `discover`, `obligations` and `conflicts` as in §C.9. The verification plan MUST be frozen at launch, bound to the hashes of its sources and stored in the control plane.

The verification modes MUST be the closed set `required`, `plan`, `off`, with the default `required`. The verification gate MUST run before the critic; when it fails the engine writes the feedback itself and does not call the critic. Derivation of a launch contract MUST state the mode it sets and MUST prefer `required` where commands are declared.
The check manifest derived on a relaunch MUST be compared with the stored one. A difference MUST become a fact for the critic, and the stored manifest MUST apply.

requirements.text: An event sink MUST offer `open`, `write`, `flush`, `close` and `status` as in §C.10, and the context of `open` MUST hold what §C.10 lists. A sink MUST receive an event only after the primary writer has written it, already redacted. A failure of a sink MUST NOT change the outcome of a run or the primary event file.

It MUST write to files of their own and never to the primary stream. It MUST be on under the `parity` profile and under `compat.legacyEvents`, and off otherwise. It MUST be byte-identical to the baseline on the fixtures of the oracle after normalization; there is no such promise elsewhere.

A secret in configuration MUST be a reference; an inline value MUST be a configuration error that refuses the launch. A `file:` target MUST lie outside the workspace and MUST be readable by its owner only.

For the audience `distributed`, auth tier 2 MUST be the default for the providers whose auth tier 1 is confirmed for personal use only, and auth tier 1 for them MUST be an opt-in marked "personal use only".

The runtime MUST use the strongest level available and MUST announce and record it for every run. C0 MUST need an opt-in in user configuration, which the environment, a flag and project configuration MUST NOT give; a proposer whose ceiling is C0 MUST be refused at launch without it. The runtime MUST never assert a sandbox by itself; only under the `parity` profile the harness adapter sets the as-is assertion variable where the baseline sets it.

The run MUST then say `protection=detect`.

At auth tier 2 a call MUST use a throwaway home built from an overlay of §C.16. Session state MUST live per phase attempt and MUST be removed when the phase attempt ends.

requirements.text: The loop-layer interface MUST have the eight call points of §D.1, called by the engine in the fixed order, and the closed set of directives of §D.1. The engine, and never a layer, MUST execute and account for every directive.

Layers MUST stack in a fixed order, to a depth of at most 2 in Wave 1. At every call point the outer layer MUST be called first and the inner layer only when the outer one returns `none`. Each layer MUST have a ledger namespace of its own.

A layer MUST declare the directives and the services it uses. The engine MUST refuse at registration a layer that declares one the engine does not offer. The harness port MUST declare `concurrentSessions`; a group MUST run only on a tested harness adapter that declares it.

A layer MUST NOT be able to write an approval, a verdict, feedback, a hint or a recovery marker; to change a counter of the outer loop; to hold a harness; to write an event or a ledger record except through the engine; or to write the project's repository. The build MUST prove it on the package graph of every layer.

With no unit of work declared in a phase attempt, a layer MUST execute nothing and MUST add nothing to any prompt but its protocol block; until the layer is engaged, a time limit of a pass and a command of the runtime MUST NOT differ from the classic loop. In a run whose verification gate does not execute (mode `plan` or `off`) the layer MUST be off, announced with the reason `gate-not-executing`.

requirements.text: A pass that ends at a valid checkpoint MUST leave the short-pass counter as it was; a pass with a valid checkpoint and a changed tree MUST be given back, so that it does not raise the pass count, and MUST spend one cycle of the layer's own cap; the exact argument lists of the inner check set MUST be exempt from the process-level repeat counter. A worker pass MUST be outside the pass loop, MUST spend no pass of the pass limit and MUST change no counter of the outer loop.

requirements.text: The closing check MUST be its own switch, `loop.micro.closing_check`, on by default. It MUST run only in a phase attempt in which a unit of work was declared, inside the cycle cap, and MUST return the proposer to work at most twice. From the moment phase evidence exists, a limit or a breaker of the pass loop MUST NOT stop the run.

requirements.text: The tree-store service MUST offer exactly the seven operations `snapshot`, `materialize`, `changed`, `compose`, `apply`, `release` and `sweep`. It MUST offer no restore, no reset and no checkout of the workspace, and an operation other than `apply` MUST NOT be able to write a path of the workspace. The interface is reserved in EP-04 major 1; Wave 1 builds only what parallel units need.

requirements.text: Integration MUST be composition and never a merge of content: the composed tree is the base in which each path of an accepted delta holds the content of that worker's final snapshot. The path sets of accepted deltas MUST be pairwise disjoint; a delta that shares a path with an earlier one in the order of the tasks at launch MUST be refused with the reason `overlap`. A model MUST NOT take part in integration.

Snapshot commits MUST exist only in the store, which lies outside the project's repository. They MUST have a fixed author, date and message, MUST never be a parent of a commit of the project, MUST never be pushed, and MUST be removed with the run. An operation of the store or of a layer MUST NOT write a file under the project's repository directory, create a reference there or change the project's index. The store MUST be unwritable by any worker; each worker tree MUST hold a repository of its own that borrows the objects of the store read-only.
requirements.parity: off (row 20 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Inside a phase attempt the runtime MUST never commit to, revert, reset, clean or check out the workspace, and MUST write nothing under the project's repository directory except the approval commit that exists at the baseline. With parallel units on, and only then, the runtime MAY make exactly two writes to the workspace: (1) the application of the composed delta of a group — forward only, only paths of audited deltas, only onto a workspace equal to the base, recorded before it is made, never undone, nothing under the repository directory; (2) the ticks of the integrated tasks, through the spec-format adapter. (Rule IR-60 as amended.)

requirements.text: After the application the engine MUST run the inner check set of the phase on the workspace, once per group, through the check runner. A failure MUST go to serial repair by the proposer in the ordinary loop; the applied changes MUST NOT be reverted. A result obtained in a worker tree or a merge check MUST NOT replace an execution at the verification gate, which runs in full on the workspace before the critic. The partial work of a killed worker MUST be discarded and its task returns to the serial loop.

The parallel plan MUST hold the fields of §D.3, MUST be computed at launch as a pure function of the task list as read at launch and of configuration, and MUST be stored in the control plane with its hash. A relaunch that derives a different plan MUST announce the difference and use the stored plan. A stored plan whose hash does not match MUST switch the layer off for the run with an integrity event. The plan MUST be printed only with the option on.
requirements.parity: off (no plan file exists) (row 20 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: `loop.parallel.units` MUST default to `off`. `loop.parallel.workers` MUST default to 2. Its ceiling MUST be the key `loop.parallel.workersMax`, a whole number of 1 or more that MUST default to 4 and MUST be a widening key: project configuration may lower it and never raise it, and a higher value in project configuration is ignored with a launch message and a doctor warning, as F100-FR-202 says for a widening key. A value of `loop.parallel.workers` above the ceiling in force MUST be a configuration error at launch. `loop.parallel.quota_headroom` MUST default to 70 per cent. `loop.parallel.allow_detect` MUST default to off and MUST be a widening key.
requirements.parity: `loop.parallel.units` off (rows 20, 21, 22, 23 and 130 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Information about groups or workers MUST NOT reach a critic-class call: no worker id, no group id, no count, no outcome of a worker, no order of integration, and no word that tells a group from a serial unit of work that named the same tasks. An integrated group MUST appear in the fact block as one unit. The two integrity kinds that parallel units add MUST be neutral: `tree-changed-outside-pass` and `protected-change-not-applied`, reported by kind and without a count. A worker tree MUST NOT exist when a critic-class call starts.

The router MUST be one pure function over a versioned rule table with the three decision points of §D.4. It MUST run nothing, read no critic prompt, no nonce and no verdict, change no role and no counter of the outer loop, and MUST NOT be able to switch a layer on. The router prototype's modes that run a phase without a critic MUST NOT exist.

Escalation MUST be its own switch, `loop.escalation`, on by default. The second repair of a unit of work MAY run on the next model tier of the same harness, in a fresh session, never on a rung that equals a critic-class call of the run in model and in effort (the signal `targetIsCriticModel`), capped at 1 per task and 2 per phase attempt, inside the cap of repairs. A rung that shares the model of a critic-class call and differs in effort is not a collision: it MAY be used, and the critic-diversity warning MUST be raised and recorded. When the quota of the target is exhausted the escalation MUST be skipped, the repair MUST run on the base model, and the skip MUST be recorded.

requirements.text: A prompt block provider MUST offer the one operation `blocks` of §D.5. One assembler MUST budget the whole prompt. With the as-is block set, which the `parity` profile selects, the prompt MUST equal the baseline's byte for byte.
requirements.parity: the as-is block set (row 12 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Carry-over MUST consist of the ledger, a handoff that the runtime writes at the start of every pass and never reads back, and the obligations index, which replaces the block of inherited verification obligations in the proposer's prompt only. Each MUST have its own switch (`carry.ledger_handoff`, `carry.index`), on by default, and the cache-stable start of the prompt likewise.
requirements.parity: off (rows 8, 9, 12 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The yield artifact MUST hold the fields of §D.6 and MUST be read as a claim under the rules of annex B §B.2. The predicate `command` MUST be refused unless the consumer allowed it. A worker of a parallel group MUST NOT yield; its yield artifact is refused.

The first-failure predicate MUST be its own switch, `verification.failfast`, on by default; it MUST NOT ride on the switch of a loop layer. The runtime MUST stop a job only if it launched the job and the yield declared `stop`; otherwise the wait ends and the job runs on. The default of `on_first_failure` MUST be `stop`; `continue-and-notify` as the default is an option that is off. The polite stop (an interrupt before a termination, with a grace period) MUST be its own switch, `carry.polite_stop`, on by default.
requirements.parity: off (rows 4, 5, 11 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The fact block MUST hold the fields of §D.7 and nothing from the list of what is never in the block. Every text in it that comes from the workspace MUST be escaped, cut, stripped of control characters and printed inside a data boundary with a token of the call. Test counts MUST NOT be shown in Wave 1, only counts of suppression markers. File modification times stay in the grounding snapshot.

When files of the protected set were changed without authority, the verification gate MUST still run, its result MUST carry the condition, and the critic MUST be told. Approval stays possible and the run MUST NOT halt. At phase entry the tree MUST be compared with the approved tree of the phase before; a difference is a fact for the critic and never blocks.

requirements.text: There MUST be one check manifest per phase, written when the loop strategy is not `classic` or when one of the switches of rows 6, 7, 31 and 33 of annex X §X.7 is on, and never under the `parity` profile. It MUST be derived at launch from the sources the verification gate uses and from nothing else, stored in the control plane with its hash, and verified before every check. It MUST hold deterministic commands only. The router MAY order and exclude among its entries; nothing MAY add an entry after launch.

requirements.text: The engine MUST judge every phase gate through the critic strategy seam and plan every phase attempt through the attempt planner seam, with the operations `judge` and `next` of §E.1. Wave 1 MUST ship one critic; a critic ensemble and human approvals are not part of Wave 1.

Every critic call MUST carry a nonce of 64 bits of its own. The nonce MUST never be written to disk, to an event or to a span before the call has returned; afterwards only its hash MUST be recorded in events, spans, the ledger and the approval record. The verdict record and the feedback of the phase attempt MAY hold the nonce in clear after the call has returned, as at the baseline, because the oracle compares them.

The model-tier bump MUST be an option, off by default: after K rejections of one phase by the critic, the next phase attempt runs on the next model tier of the same harness. K and the model-tier ladder MUST come from configuration. A failed verification gate and a MALFORMED reply MUST NOT count towards K. A target that equals a critic-class call of the run in model and in effort, and a target whose quota is exhausted, MUST be skipped. A target that shares the model of a critic-class call and differs from it in effort is not a collision (ruling 49): it MAY be used, and the critic-diversity warning MUST be raised and recorded, as for escalation (F100-FR-130). The bump and the escalation of annex D §D.4 MUST be separate rules with separate counts.
requirements.assumption: CQ-204; CQ-191 (ruling 49 is read to allow a target on the critic's model at another effort, with the warning, for the bump as for escalation)
