requirements.text: A run MUST be in exactly one of the ten written states of §E.2. `dead`, `stale` and `launch-abandoned` MUST be derived by readers and never written. A quota pause MUST be a state and never a stop. `blocked-on-human` MUST be a resting state: no process, the lock released, left only by `resume`.

The only transitions of a run MUST be T1 to T18 of §E.2, each written by the process the table names. A host MUST write no transition. The CLI MUST write only transitions into and out of `created` (T1, T2, T3, T17).

The run record MUST hold the fields of §E.2, among them the containment level, the result of the proof that the critic holds no tools or only read-only tools, and the version of the redaction pattern set. It MUST have one writer.
requirements.assumption: CQ-019 (field names; the sources name the content)

requirements.text: A run that cannot go on without the consumer MUST emit the event `blocked` with a reason from the closed set of §E.2 and what it needs, write the terminal record with the stop reason and the exit code of the table of blocked reasons, release the lock and end. It MUST NOT be relaunched by either relaunch classifier table.
requirements.assumption: CQ-020 (which existing stop reason each blocked reason ends with; the sources say "an existing stop reason" and name none except for the wait ceiling)

requirements.text: When `resume`, or a `launch` that continues a run, finds a changed source hash, the CLI MUST refuse with exit 3, name the file, and record the refusal in the launch record (T3). Readers MUST show the run as `blocked-on-human` with the attention item `source-changed`. The event `blocked` for it MUST be written by the next process that becomes the writer of the event file, marked as synthesized.
requirements.parity: no check at `resume` (the check is at critic start) (row 15 of annex X §X.7)
requirements.assumption: CQ-021 (who writes the state and the event at a refused `resume`, since the CLI is not a writer of run state or of the event file)

requirements.text: A quota pause MUST spend no reject, no pass, no MALFORMED count, no error count, no wall-clock budget and no relaunch budget. It MUST hold while the runtime lives. It MUST have a ceiling, `pause.maxTotalMs`, that the consumer can set, with the default of 24 hours; at the ceiling the run MUST rest in `blocked-on-human` with the stop reason `paused_quota_ceiling`. After a reboot nothing relaunches by itself; `resume` enters the pause again.
requirements.parity: not observable (row 39 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The engine MUST verify the lease at every boundary at which it reads the stop request. When the owner of the lease is lost, the engine MUST finish the current pass, run no phase gate, write its terminal record with the cause `owner-lost`, the stop reason `stop_flag` and `causedBy: crash`, and exit 6.

The stop reasons of the product MUST be exactly the 15 members of §E.3, each with its engine exit code and its attribute `transient`. The terminal record MUST carry one of them on every exit that has a member in the column "Stop reasons" of the engine table of §E.4. On an exit that has none (0, 5, 70, and the causes of 1 and 3 without a member) the field MUST be null, `retryable` MUST be false, and an as-is stop line MUST NOT be written. A reader that finds another value MUST treat the stop as not retryable and report it.

The compatibility projection MUST keep writing the as-is stop line with the as-is literal for every member 1 to 14. Where the engine and the pass loop both write a reason for one stop, the projection MUST hold two lines with different fields, the engine's line being the newer one, and the line of the pass loop MUST carry the as-is iteration field. The only outcome literal of the as-is end line MUST be `all_approved`. The four literals that learning reads as arbitration signals (`max_rejects`, `gate_oscillation`, `critic_config`, `proposer_no_progress`) MUST keep their meaning.
requirements.parity: on (the projection is compared) (row 17 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The closed families that are not stop reasons MUST be kept with their as-is literals, each listed in annex X §X.6: the kill reasons of the watchdogs with their class (`idle_timeout`: hang; `repeat_stall`, `progress_stall`: futility; `hard_cap`: budget); the stage reasons, transient (`exit`, `timeout`, `recovery-deadline`, `recovery-exhausted`) and deliberate (`postcondition`, `stage-precondition`, `setup-required`, `interrupted`, `existing-prerequisite`, `completed`, and `exec-error:` with a detail); the pipeline exit reasons (`preflight`, `all-stages-complete`, or a stage reason); the refusals of the launch checks; the relaunch refusals and the approval `classified-transient`.

The engine MUST exit with exactly the codes of the table "Engine" of §E.4, and every cause of a halt MUST map to exactly one code. The mapping from the result of the pass loop MUST apply only when phase evidence is absent.

Every termination of a run MUST map to exactly one of the seven codes 0 to 6 of the engine, with the meanings done 0, internal 1, rejects 2, spec 3, budget 4, lock 5, stop 6, which is the vocabulary that the Specstride baseline and Lisa share. Code 70 is for an uncaught error of a command and is not a termination of a run.

The pass loop, the critic call, the verification gate inside the engine and the internal helpers MUST return result records whose `exit_code` carries the numbers of §E.4. Where the baseline prints such a number, compatibility output MUST print the same number.

The engine MUST have two start modes. In `standalone` it takes the workspace lock, writes the lease and the run record, and owns the transitions of the root. In `child` it verifies the lease handed down by the root and never takes a lock. The executable of the engine MUST be resolved at launch and pinned by path and hash in the launch record, from a configuration key whose default is the product's own entry.
requirements.parity: the oracle sets the key to its engine stub where a fixture needs one (row 41 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: A run MUST be a detached tree of processes as in §F.1: one runtime root per launch, and the engine as its child. The root MUST NOT be connected to the host after the handshake: no pipe, no socket the host must keep, no parent that waits. A run MUST NOT depend on a host hook, a monitor or a host process.
requirements.status: unverified (check: the spike starts the root from the host's shell tool in an interactive session and in headless mode, with the shell sandbox off and on, on Linux and macOS, ends the session, and confirms that the root lives; verified-on: —; pin: host versions of the spike)

requirements.text: There MUST be one lock per workspace, taken by the runtime root and handed down to the engine as a lease; a child MUST never take a second lock. A second pipeline on a held workspace MUST end with the pipeline code 24 at launch. A foreground `specstride run` on a held workspace MUST end with the engine code 5.

The launcher MUST be a file the operator can see and run, whose only job is to call the pipeline entry with the hash of the launch bundle. The runtime root MUST verify the hash of the launch bundle and the launcher's own hash at launch and at every relaunch, and MUST refuse an edited launcher.

When the engine ends with a code outside 0 to 6, or by a signal, the runtime root MUST write a synthesized terminal record with the cause `crash`, end every `owned` process, and consult its relaunch classifier. When the runtime root itself dies, or the machine reboots, a relaunch MUST NOT happen by itself in Wave 1: the run reads as `dead`, and `resume` reclaims the lock, closes the dead launch with a synthesized end event, and continues at the first phase without a valid approval record. When the owner is dead and an `owned` process group is alive, `resume` MUST refuse and name the survivors.

The runtime root MUST accept exactly the two kinds of run request of §F.2. A request of kind `engine` MUST have the same lock, lease, relaunch classifier and digest as one of kind `pipeline`, and no launch contract to validate.

A launch MUST follow the four steps of §F.3 and MUST end in exactly one of the outcomes `started`, `attached`, `refused`. Readiness MUST be confirmed by the lease that carries the launch nonce, whatever the detach strategy. An unanswered launch MUST be closed as `launch-abandoned` by the next launch.

Re-attachment MUST be reading only. A new host session MUST learn of a run through `status` or through a host hook shim that prints a precomputed status line. The line MUST carry `validUntil`, which is `none`, without expiry, for a run that rests and has no lease; when a time is given and has passed the shim MUST print that the state is unknown and name the command `status`.

`relaunch.owner` MUST be ordinary configuration with the values `root` and `supervise` and the default `root`. Both relaunch classifier tables MUST be pure tables evaluated by the table evaluator. A relaunch MUST always start a fresh session and MUST carry counts and ids from the ledger.
requirements.parity: `supervise` (row 14 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Each relaunch classifier table MUST NOT relaunch a run whose terminal record says `retryable: false`, a run in `blocked-on-human`, a run that was stopped on request, or a run while `hold-relaunch` is in force. A quota pause MUST give the classifier nothing to classify. A run in `blocked-on-human` MUST NOT be relaunched under any profile, the `parity` profile included: the row of table 1 (`relaunch-observe`, feature 123) that refuses it, O-33, is active under every profile. Under the `parity` profile only the row of table 1 that refuses a stop with `retryable: false`, O-34, is inactive (row 132 of annex X §X.7; DV-114): there table 1 classifies a stopped launcher that is not blocked as the baseline does, from the listed exit codes and the allowed stop reasons only.
requirements.parity: table 1 reads the blocked reason (row O-33) and does not read `retryable` (row O-34 inactive; row 132 of annex X §X.7)
requirements.assumption: CQ-238 (answered by the owner on 2026-09-30: the row of table 1 that refuses a blocked run is active under every profile; register row DV-114 covers the row that refuses a stop that is not retryable only)

requirements.text: The lock and liveness provider MUST offer `acquire`, `heartbeat`, `release`, `probe`, `reclaim`, `handDown` and `verify` with the results and errors of §F.5. A foreign owner MUST never be reclaimed automatically. The as-is lock fallback that was never released MUST NOT be carried.
requirements.status: unverified (check: the provider's conformance suite on macOS; verified-on: —; pin: —)

requirements.text: A detach strategy MUST offer `available`, `start` and `describe` as in §F.6. The product MUST work with the strategy `foreground` wherever `spawn-detached` does not survive the end of a host session.
requirements.status: unverified (check: the spike of the detached runtime, as in F100-FR-155; verified-on: —; pin: —)

requirements.text: Stage kinds and precondition checks MUST be registries with the five and the six built-in entries of §F.7. The schema of the launch contract MUST name a kind by id and MUST NOT hold a closed list of kinds.
requirements.assumption: CQ-022 (the names of the operations `validate`, `run` and `evaluate`; the sources give the two registries and their built-in entries only)

requirements.text: A key that the launch contract pins MUST take the value of the launch contract in every child of the runtime root, and the value from the shell MUST be stripped. This MUST apply to the learning mode, to the bound of learning decisions, and to live output in a run without a terminal, and to no other key.
requirements.parity: as at the baseline (the two as-is keys only) (rows 38, 43 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The runtime root and the pipeline entry MUST exit with exactly the codes of §F.8. Each class of failure of the launcher MUST map to one distinct code: 20 invalid, 21 preflight, 22 stage, 23 stale, 24 lock.

With `relaunch.owner: root` the runtime root stays alive after a failed stage, so the code 22 MUST be the code with which the root finally exits when it does not relaunch, and the pipeline state and the digest MUST show the same values as with `supervise`.
requirements.parity: `supervise` (the root exits at the failed stage) (row 14 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The CLI MUST implement protocol 1 of §G.1 and MUST print the integer 1, and nothing else, for `specstride --protocol`. A host package MUST compare the integer with the range it supports and MUST refuse a mismatch with one line that names the doctor. A change that removes or renames a command, a flag, a line or a field of `--json` output MUST raise the integer.

Of the module entry points of the Specstride baseline, exactly three MUST be public commands, with the exit codes of the baseline: `spec`, `verify` and `learn`. The pass loop and the critic MUST NOT be commands; their codes are fields of result records (annex E §E.4).

Every command that prints facts MUST offer `--json`. Its output MUST be one record with a `schema` field (in compatibility output `events --json` prints one record per line, as the baseline does), in a stable order of keys, without escape sequences for colour, and without a secret value, an account identifier or a token. `--json` and `--verbose` MUST be opt-in.

`resume` MUST accept a flag by which the consumer accepts an intended change of spec, plan or task list. With the flag, `resume` MUST derive the verification plan and the check manifest again, record the new hashes in the run snapshot, keep the counts and the phase evidence of phases already delivered, and emit an event that every critic of the run receives as a fact. Without the flag, `resume` MUST refuse with exit 3 and name the changed file. The flag MUST be spelled `--accept-source-change`.
requirements.parity: not used (row 15 of annex X §X.7)
requirements.assumption: CQ-017 (the name of the flag; ruling P12 leaves it to be settled)

requirements.text: A command MUST NOT have a flag that switches off a launch check, the terms gate or a budget cap. The consumer's comment MUST only select among options that validation of the launch contract accepts. Anything that widens scope or spend MUST need a flag or a configuration key set by the consumer, and MUST never be inferred from text.

The CLI MUST have exactly the two output modes of §G.2. Compatibility output MUST reproduce every as-is line byte for byte, including the literal for an absent child exit code, the quoting of the old language in the relaunch line, and the hold line on every unchanged poll.
requirements.parity: compatibility output (row 18 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: A line that has no as-is equivalent MUST never be written to a stream that the oracle compares with the reference. Under the `parity` profile the product MUST print no such line on any stream. Outside it, a new line MUST be printed only when the feature it belongs to is on.
requirements.parity: no new line (row 19 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Text from outside the runtime (feedback of the critic, names of tests, messages of a harness) MUST never be echoed into default output. Default output MUST refer to it by logical name. Every message that names state MUST name it by logical name; a message that at the baseline carried a physical path of state is compared through the layout table.

Every labelled line of the product MUST follow the grammar of §G.3. Feature 100 owns the grammar; each line belongs to the feature that prints it, which specifies its keys and values inside the grammar. A label of one family MUST never be used by another family.

The `[LOOP]` line MUST be printed before the digest, in default output only, and only when a loop layer is on or was switched off by rule with an announced reason. Its `parallel=` fields MUST be printed only with parallel units on. It MUST never be printed under the `parity` profile.
requirements.parity: not printed (rows 19, 20 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: The digest MUST be the final line of every run of the pipeline entry, with the grammar of §G.3. The runtime MUST produce it from events; a host skill MUST print it verbatim.

Messages and records that at the baseline name an implementation file MUST name a logical component instead, through the component-name table of annex X §X.8. The text after the name MUST be equal to the baseline's.

Every command MUST exit with exactly the codes of its row in §G.4. A usage error MUST keep the as-is code of its command. An uncaught error of any command MUST exit 70. An unknown first argument (verb) MUST exit 1; an unknown sub-verb of a command exits with the code of the row of that command.
requirements.assumption: CQ-201 ("unknown subcommand" is read as an unknown first argument only)

requirements.text: `resume` MUST refuse with exit 5 when the lock is held, with exit 3 when there is nothing to resume, and with exit 3 when the hash of the spec, of the plan or of the task list changed since launch. For the task list the hash that ignores checkboxes MUST be compared, so that a tick never refuses a resume.
requirements.parity: the oracle maps the as-is code 1 to 5 and to 3; the refusal for a changed source has no reference (row 15 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Supervision MUST end with one of seven outcomes, each mapped to one exit code: completed 0, stopped 2, unknown-terminal 3, refused 4, supervision-expired 5, failed 22, lock-conflict 24. The double uses of the baseline MUST be kept: 2 also for a usage error, 4 also for the launch decision `attach`.

The doctor MUST exit 0 when no finding has the severity `fail`, 1 when it could not run, 2 when at least one finding has the severity `fail`, and 3 on a usage error. With `--strict` a warning MUST exit 2. A probe that times out inside a check MUST never raise the code above that of a warning.

The commands that have no as-is equivalent (`launch`, `wait`, `state export`, `state import`, `state adopt`, `harness verify`, `config show`, `config schema`, `tripwire clear`) MUST exit with the codes of their rows in §G.4.
requirements.assumption: CQ-023 (the codes of commands that have no as-is equivalent, other than those of `launch` after the handshake; the sources give none)

requirements.text: The output of every command that a host skill calls MUST stay inside the byte limit that its owner derives from the budgets of §G.5. The build MUST measure bytes and MUST fail on a breach. The budget for a whole run holds with `relaunch.owner: root`; with `supervise` the host watches for the whole run and the budget is not promised.

The read model MUST offer the pure operations `project` and `reduce` of §G.6, and a cursor held by the caller. The event stream and the named state files MUST be its only inputs. An attention item for a run that is blocked on a human MUST name what the run needs, and for a changed source the file.
The doctor MUST be a registry of checks with the form of §G.7, and its `--json` output MUST follow the schema of §G.7. The launch checks MUST be exactly the checks whose flag `lb` is set.

The launch contract MUST follow the schema of §G.8, and that one schema MUST also be the validator. A launch contract MUST be promoted only by validation. A validated launch contract without a matching proof of promotion, and one whose sources changed, MUST be refused with the pipeline codes 20 and 23. A top-level key the schema does not hold MUST refuse the launch contract.

The host skill `specstride-run` MUST launch by default. Its modes MUST be `run` and `dry-run`. `dry-run` MUST withhold the launch and print the plan. The as-is mode names MUST map: `generate` to `dry-run`; `run` and `auto` to `run`.
requirements.parity: mapped through the mode map (row 37 of annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: Derivation MUST expose judgment as the exchange of §G.9, which feature 107 implements as the derivation half of EP-01: the CLI inventories, and the host judges batches of at most 3,000 tokens. A host without a model MAY delegate the judgment to a harness named in user configuration, through the `completion` level; the delegation MUST be recorded in the digest. The host MUST never need to open the launch contract or the sources.
requirements.assumption: CQ-024 (the schema id `specstride.judgment/1` and the three steps come from the red team of the architecture; the architecture file names the delegation only)

requirements.text: The front door MUST reach the presenter only through the interface of §G.10, and the presenter MUST read nothing but the stream of events and the settings it is handed. The presenter MUST never change the exit code of a command, MUST never write state, and MUST be best-effort: a failure of the presenter MUST NOT stall or fail a run.
requirements.assumption: CQ-101; CQ-121 (the interface is new: the split of feature 119 needs it, and no source states it)

requirements.text: A host package MUST offer `describe`, `renderSkill`, `renderEntry` and `evalDriver.run`, and MAY offer `renderStatusHooks`, as in §H.1. It MUST declare every capability of the table of capabilities, and the product MUST use the declared fallback for each absent one.

The product MUST have two host skills with the logical ids `specstride-run` and `specstride-reverse`, and a doctor skill. A host skill MUST be a thin layer over the CLI: it MUST be operable without reading the product's source, its state or a launch contract, and its happy path MUST need no reference file.
Each host skill MUST stay inside its token budget of annex G §G.5, and the build MUST enforce it by measuring bytes.

Invoking the host skill `specstride-run` MUST be the consumer's consent to launch. The consumer's optional comment MUST steer the run and MUST NOT be able to bypass a launch check, the terms gate or a budget. The host skill MUST say what it changed because of the comment.
A host package MUST never install or update the CLI without the consumer noticing. On a missing or mismatched CLI it MUST report through the doctor and print the command to run.
requirements.status: unverified (check: every fact about host behaviour that comes from documentation only, among them the lifetime of a background host hook, is captured on a live host; verified-on: —; pin: host version of the capture)

requirements.text: Every event MUST carry the envelope of §X.1, with typed values, null for an unknown value and absence for a value that does not apply. `seq` MUST be given by the one writer at the append. `workerId` and `wseq` MUST be absent on the main line. A run with parallel units on MUST still record `strategy` as `micro`.

A change inside a major of the event schema MUST be additive. A reader MUST ignore a field and an event type it does not know, MUST tolerate a torn last line, and MUST declare the range of majors it accepts; an event outside the range MUST give a doctor warning and never a failure of a run. Event types that start with `x.` MUST be free for third parties. Every event type MUST have a row in the table of the compatibility projection, a row that projects to nothing included.

An event MUST NOT hold content. Content MUST be referred to by logical name, hash and size. Every free-text field of an event MUST pass the redactor and MUST be cut to a size cap. Liveness MUST never be an event. Every event that opens something MUST have a matching event that closes it; where a process died before it could write the closing event, the next writer MUST write it, marked as synthesized.

Configuration MUST be resolved per key through the eight ranks of §X.2. The as-is file at the install root MUST NOT be read. The resolved value of every key MUST be recorded with the rank it came from.

Every key MUST have one of the trust classes of §X.2. Project configuration MUST be able to narrow a run and never to widen it. A widening key in project configuration MUST be ignored with a launch message and a doctor warning.

A configuration file MUST carry `schema`. An unknown key MUST be an error that refuses the launch; a key under `x-` MUST be ignored. An inline secret MUST be an error. The as-is names of environment variables MUST stay as aliases of keys, through the alias table of §X.8. A value that arrives through an alias of an as-is variable and that the baseline reads late MUST, under the `parity` profile, fail where the baseline fails and not at launch; the owner of the key states the place.

There MUST be one table evaluator, used by the router, the quota classifier, both relaunch classifier tables, lane derivation, the terms gate and the attempt planner. It MUST be a pure function: no I/O, no clock, no randomness, no model. For every vector of signals exactly one row MUST fire: rows are tried in order and the first whose predicate holds fires; a table without a default row for a decision point MUST fail validation at load. Every decision MUST be recorded with its rule id and the version of the table. The bump table of the attempt planner MUST have the same form, with the one decision point `attempt-tier`, which belongs to the attempt planner and not to the router.
requirements.assumption: CQ-025 (the set of operators of a predicate, and first-match order; the sources give "an ordered table", "a predicate over named signals" and "exactly one row fires")

requirements.text: There MUST be one redactor and one point of redaction, at the ingress of annex A F100-FR-009. Every sink (event file, exporters, digest, status, read model) MUST receive the redacted form. The redactor MUST replace every exact occurrence of a registered secret value and every match of the versioned pattern set, which is data. It MUST fail closed: when it cannot run, the content is dropped and the record says so. The consumer's comment MUST pass the redactor before it is recorded.
Before the runtime makes a commit, the files of the commit that the runtime wrote MUST be scanned for registered secrets and for the patterns. A hit MUST block the commit and raise an event.

There MUST be one hashing scheme, offered by one hasher with the operations of §X.5, and every feature that hashes a source, a launch contract, a plan or a manifest MUST use it. Hashes over fixture content MUST equal the baseline's. A feature that ports a hash that a baseline takes over a record MUST state which form the baseline hashes: the canonical record text as it is (the content hash of the canonical record text; for example the verification plan, its source projection, its ids and the project fingerprint of the Specstride baseline, F105-FR-011, F105-FR-012), or the text with a final line end (the canonical record hash; for example the launch contract, F107-FR-019). No feature MUST build a record text of its own. The word "hash" MUST be used for every such value; the as-is word survives only in literals of the compatibility projection. The classification of the staleness verdict MUST be the one operation of the hasher that §X.5 names: a pure function of the recorded hashes and the hashes now, which every feature that decides staleness (102, 103, 104) MUST call and MUST NOT reimplement; the reading of the files and of the task lines stays with `@specstride/spec-formats`, and EP-03 gains no operation.
requirements.assumption: CQ-214 (the classification moves into the hasher module of the kernel, owner of its rules 104)

requirements.text: Every closed set of the product MUST have a row in the table of §X.6, with its owner, whether an owner decision or the design closes it, and what a reader does with an unknown value. Where the table points to the specification of the owner for the members, that specification MUST list them all. A feature that introduces a closed set MUST state these facts in its own specification under the heading "Closed sets", so that the row can be added here.
A static test MUST fail when a closed set of the `contracts` package has no row in §X.6, when a row names a member the package does not hold, or when a reader has no branch for an unknown value.

The product MUST ship the named profile `parity` as versioned data with one row per switch, as in §X.7. Selecting the profile MUST set every switch to its value of the column "Under `parity`" and MUST do nothing else. The profile MUST be selected by ordinary configuration.
requirements.parity: the profile itself (annex X §X.7)

requirements.text: For every switch of the product the profile MUST hold a value. A test MUST fail when a switch exists that the profile does not hold. The second suite of the oracle MUST be the profile `parity` with row 1 set to `micro` and nothing else changed: it compares compatibility output, as the first suite does, so the `[LOOP]` line and the status line are not reachable in it and are proven by the tests of their own features.
requirements.assumption: CQ-028 (whether the second suite compares compatibility output or default output; F100-FR-211 and register row DV-034 read differently)

requirements.text: A feature that introduces a switch MUST state in its specification, in the field `parity:` of the requirement and in a table "Rows of the `parity` profile", the switch, its default, its value under `parity`, and the register row. The value under `parity` MUST be the one that reproduces the as-is behaviour; where no as-is behaviour exists, it MUST be "off" or "not used". The row is added to §X.7 under the next free number. A feature MUST NOT change a row of another feature.

The normalization rules MUST be exactly N-01 to N-29 of §X.8. A rule MUST be added only with a row of the divergence register, or with a statement that the value is not deterministic in the reference itself. A rule that replaces nothing in any fixture MUST fail the suite. N-02 MUST apply to the text of messages as well as to captured trees.

The layout tables (old side and new side), the environment alias table, the component-name table, the mode map, the exit-code map of `resume` and the key-name map of the launch contract MUST be versioned data of the normalization contract. The new side of the layout table MUST be the table of annex B §B.5. The old side MUST cover every `file` row of the behaviour inventory that has a kept disposition. A registry entry of the baseline that the port does not carry MUST be treated by rule N-15 as §X.8 states under the component-name table: found at run time, taken out before storage and comparison, and named in no stored capture.
requirements.assumption: CQ-026 (the logical component names; and the old side of the layout table is given here for the paths that two or more features compare, the complete list being delivered as data with the plan); CQ-029 (how a reference output is compared that lists registry entries, one of which the port does not carry)

requirements.text: The port MUST read the variables of the hermetic environment of the oracle, or a documented mapping of them that is part of the normalization contract. Stub transcripts MUST be a compared surface, in a form that is neutral to the transport of the critic.

The threat model of the product MUST be the 49 threats of §X.9 with the five structural controls. The feature named as owner MUST specify the control of each threat and its test. A feature that weakens a control MUST report it as a contradiction with feature 100.

A version of a published package MUST be published only by the build, from a protected branch of the repository of the product, and MUST carry an attestation that binds the package to the commit and to the build that made it. A version MUST NOT be published from a working copy or by hand. The release check MUST fail for a version that lacks the attestation or whose attestation names another repository, branch or commit. This is the control of threat T-43; the host package cites it (owner 113 for the host package).
requirements.status: unverified (check: the attestation of a published version is read back from the package registry and names the repository, the branch and the commit of the build; verified-on: —; pin: the first published version)

requirements.text: A component outside the runtime tree MUST NOT be able to create, change or remove control state, apart from what the CLI writes: inbox requests, launch records with the comment beside them, the supervision record, the run snapshot and the resolved registry at launch, the launch contract and its launch bundle, and the source inventory and the verification commands of a reverse run. Every one of these inputs MUST be validated by the runtime before it acts on it.
Every run MUST record the three per-run fields that F100-FR-143 names for the run record, as that requirement states them; this requirement adds no field.

A secret value MUST NOT appear in any event, span, digest line, status output or payload of the read model. A test MUST plant canary secrets in the prompt, in the reply of the model, in tool arguments, in tool output, in phase evidence, in the output of a check and in the consumer's comment, with content capture on, and MUST assert that none appears in any sink. Passing this test MUST be a release condition.

A component of Wave 1 MUST NOT open a network listener. A later viewer MUST be started by the consumer, MUST be read-only, MUST bind to loopback only, and MUST refuse every request that lacks the token of the session or that names a foreign origin or host.

Text from outside the runtime MUST be treated as data everywhere: wrapped in random boundaries per call when it enters a prompt, never echoed into a host session by default, rendered as text, and never parsed for control records.

For each of the 19 extension points the conformance suite MUST pass on the sample implementation outside the core and on every Wave 1 implementation, with no core file changed and with the import-boundary check passing.

Under the `parity` profile the parity oracle MUST report no result `different` on any fixture family and any surface, and the second suite MUST pass with equal counters. Every parity test of every feature, those of the behaviour of dsh, Codex and prime included, MUST pass before any release.

On a reference project a run started through the host package for Claude Code MUST reach every phase gate approved, on the same build on which the oracle and the second suite pass. The run MUST be reported per stage against the measured baseline.

requirements.text: The build MUST fail when a file of the control plane has no `schema` field, when a reader accepts a different major, when a closed set has no row in §X.6, when a switch has no row in §X.7, or when a specification names state by a physical path. The check of the specifications for physical paths follows the scope rule of F100-FR-226.

A consistency review over the specifications of all features MUST find no exit code, stop reason, state name, logical name, event envelope field or configuration rank that disagrees with the annexes of feature 100, and no requirement that lists harnesses other than by reading the registry. The review MAY run scoped: the runner of the static tests takes a list of feature folders as its subject (the variable `TESTKIT_STATIC_SCOPE`, folder names separated by commas; unset means every feature) and still reads the specifications of every feature as reference, for the harness registry and the vocabulary. A phase gate of an implementation run MAY use the scoped review with the running feature as its subject, so that an edit to another feature's specification does not fail that gate. The full review over all features MUST pass in the last phase of feature 100 and before any release; the scoped review never replaces it. `TESTKIT_STATIC_SCOPE` is an input of the test runner of the `testkit` package, not a switch of the product.
